en: Mayon Volcano in Albay features a nearly perfect symmetrical stratovolcano cone built by alternating layers of hardened lava and volcanic ash.
Super Typhoon Haiyan, locally known as Yolanda, generated one-minute sustained wind speeds of 315 kilometers per hour in 2013.
Jupiter's Great Red Spot is a massive, persistent anticyclonic storm located in the planet's southern hemisphere that is wider than Earth.
The Apollo 11 astronauts landed their lunar module on the Moon's flat basaltic plain officially named the Sea of Tranquility.
Galena is a shiny, silver-colored metallic mineral that serves as the primary ore mined globally for extracting elemental lead.
The Pasig River in Manila functions as a tidal estuary, naturally connecting Laguna de Bay to Manila Bay.
The Pleiades, commonly called the Seven Sisters, is a bright open star cluster containing over a thousand stars in Taurus.
The 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo deposited thick volcanic ash that weathered into highly fertile andosol soils across Central Luzon.
The El Niño climate phenomenon warms the central Pacific Ocean, significantly reducing Philippine rainfall and causing severe dry-season droughts.
Titan is Saturn's largest moon and the only natural satellite in our solar system known to possess a dense atmosphere.
The devastating 1990 Luzon earthquake was triggered by a sudden tectonic slip along the Digdig Fault of the Philippine Fault Zone.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is a dormant stratovolcano and the highest peak in the Philippines, standing exactly 2,954 meters tall.
